thread.title: Lawrence: How will you say 'no' to Donald Trump and Stephen Miller's cruelty?
thread.title_full: Lawrence: How will you say 'no' to Donald Trump and Stephen Miller's cruelty?

author: @jonathanprimeaux1160
text: What the video frames as a “Trump administration retreat” is really Democrats losing control of the narrative they tried to manufacture through outrage politics. The White House quieting officials isn’t an admission of guilt — it’s what responsible leadership does when facts are still being gathered and investigations are ongoing. Democrats and their media allies immediately labeled the situation a moral collapse, declared federal agents “murderers,” and elevated activists and clergy to replace evidence with emotion. Instead of waiting for due process, they rushed to canonize Alex Pretti as a political symbol and weaponized his death to delegitimize federal law enforcement, border enforcement, and anyone who disagrees with their sanctuary-state ideology. This isn’t about justice — it’s about controlling the story before facts complicate it. The so-called “moral moment” promoted by Democrats is really a familiar playbook: exploit tragedy, silence disagreement, and use religious language to shame Americans into submission. While preaching compassion, the same leaders excuse riots, undermine police, block cooperation with federal authorities, and then feign shock when enforcement situations escalate. They claim to mourn Pretti while openly calling to defund or dismantle the very institutions tasked with public safety. The video’s call to “say no” is not about accountability — it’s about saying no to border enforcement, no to federal authority, and no to the rule of law unless Democrats are in charge. Republicans can acknowledge loss of life without surrendering to hysteria, and can demand real investigations without turning tragedy into a fundraising slogan or a moral cudgel. That’s the difference between governance and propaganda.
